title: Reduce KV cache thrash with dynamic reservoir allocation and staggered decode waves
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: In high-concurrency workloads, simultaneous prefill/decodes from many sessions cause synchronized KV page loads and writebacks which thrash GPU memory residency. This shows up as high eviction churn, increased tail latency, and worse throughput for mixed-sequence-length workloads.

Goal: Reduce KV eviction churn and p99 decode latency without materially increasing mean latency or reducing throughput. Approach combines a lightweight tiered reservoir allocator for KV pages plus a staggered decode wave scheduler that smooths prefill-induced I/O and memory pressure. Additionally, integrate kernel-selection hints so the runtime can pick memory-compact kernels under high-reservoir-utilization.

Key ideas: 
1) Dynamic reservoir: maintain three soft tiers (hot/warm/cold) in the paged KV system. Pages are scored by a composite reuse probability (recent accesses + prefix-match signal) and fragmentation penalty. The reservoir size adapts to overall GPU residency and recent eviction rate; when eviction churn rises, reservoir temporarily increases hot retention for high-reuse pages.
2) Fragment-aware compaction window: periodically coalesce small fragmented pages when GPU idle windows are detected (between decode waves) to reduce allocation scatter. Compaction is opportunistic and bounded to avoid CPU/GPU stalls.
3) Staggered decode waves: instead of starting all decodes/prefills immediately, a lightweight scheduler groups requests into micro-waves (10–50ms buckets) based on model/tenant affinity and predicted KV locality. Staggering prevents synchronized hard-pressure on the allocator and allows the reservoir to serve the true hot set.
4) Kernel selection integration: when reservoir utilization is high or compaction backlog grows, the kernel selector prefers memory-compact attention kernels (trading some cycles for lower working set) for the next N decodes. Kernel hints are transient and per-model-profile.

Trade-offs and reasoning: 
- We accept a small increase in some mean latency for decodes (by choosing compact kernels or slight waiting for stagger windows) to massively reduce p99s and evictions which harm throughput.
- Reservoir growth is controlled; unbounded growth would reduce capacity for other tenants, so we enforce soft caps and tenant-weighted limits.
- Compaction is done opportunistically to avoid introducing jank; if compaction causes stalls it will be throttled back.

Success metrics (targets): 
- Reduce KV eviction rate (pages/sec) by >= 30% on mixed workloads.
- p99 decode latency down by >= 20% on our standard multi-tenant replay.
- No more than 5% regression in average token throughput.

Longer-term: If effective, expose a Dedicated/Private knob for conservative vs aggressive reservoir sizing and include an autosuggest profile in Redwood Optimize based on workload fingerprinting.
acceptance_criteria: A/B tests show >=30% reduction in eviction churn for mixed short+long sequence replay on staging cluster
p99 decode latency reduction >=20% in the multi-tenant replay harness without >5% throughput regression
No regression in model output correctness or KV corruption incidents across 72h soak
Implementation includes configurable parameters (reservoir caps, wave bucket size, kernel-hint window) and rollout flags for canary
notes: Prototype approach uses a lock-free per-shard score-queue and a background compaction task triggered on idle windows
Kernel selector extension: add 'residency_pressure' signal (0..1) consumed by kernel-ranking heuristics
